paragraphs.text: Sabry et al. (1997) described 3 Bedouin sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type 1 and dysmorphic features. The features included growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail/phalangeal hypoplasia of the fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of the toes, and hallux valgus. The patients' peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures also had a very low mitotic index. The phenotype varied among the 3 sibs. Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed an association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type 1 and a specific form of distal limb anomalies. They suggested that congenital ptosis and a low mitotic index might also be part of the syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Babbs et al. (2013) used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. They identified a homozygous c.533T-A transversion in the C15ORF41 gene (CDIN1), a gene of unknown function. The mutation was predicted to cause a leu178-to-gln (L178Q) substitution. They then sequenced C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative pedigrees with the disorder. In 2 further pedigrees of SouthEast Asian origin, they found a homozygous c.281A-G transition, predicted to cause a tyr94-to-cys (Y94C) substitution. Detailed sequence similarity searches predicted that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease belonging to the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.
